title: Chicken Provençale
description: This is a recipe was picked up from Steven Stolman, a clothing and interior designer whose “Confessions of a Serial Entertainer” is a useful guide to the business and culture of dinner parties and general hospitality. It is a perfect dinner-party meal: chicken thighs or legs dusted in flour and roasted with shallots, lemons and garlic in a bath of vermouth and under a shower of herbes de Provence. They go crisp in the heat above the fat, while the shallots and garlic melt into sweetness below. You could serve with rice, or a green salad and lots of baguette to mop up the sauce.
ingredients: 4 full chicken legs or 8 bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs
2 tablespoons herbes de Provence (maybe with a little fennel, smashed or ground or powdered)
4-6 (or more!) medium-size shallots, peeled and halved
½ cup dry vermouth (or white wine/chicken broth)
directions: Season the chicken with salt and pepper. Put the flour in a shallow dish, and lightly dredge the chicken in it, shaking the pieces to remove excess flour.
Swirl the oil in a large roasting pan, and place the floured chicken in it, nicely spaced, skin side up.
Season the chicken with the herbes de Provence.
Arrange the lemons, garlic cloves and shallots around the chicken (maybe with any extra thyme sprigs), and then add the vermouth (mixture) to the pan all around the vegetables.
Put the pan in the oven, and roast for 20 to 25 minutes, then baste it generously with the pan juices.
Continue roasting for an additional 20 to 25 minutes, or until the chicken is very crisp and the meat cooked through.
Serve in the pan or on a warmed platter, garnished with the thyme.
